items.content:
이 책은 PostgreSQL이 관계형 데이터베이스를 넘어 JSON, 벡터 검색, 시계열 데이터 등 현대 애플리케이션의 다양한 워크로드를 감당할 수 있음을 실제 예제로 보여줍니다. 개발자가 기술 스택을 늘리기 전에 Postgres의 가능성을 먼저 확인하고 실무에서 효과적으로 활용하도록 돕습니다.

AI 기능 하나를 붙일 때마다 저장소가 하나씩 늘어나는 팀이 적지 않다. 검색엔진을 따로, 벡터 저장소를 따로, 메시지 큐를 또 따로 들이다 보면 운영해야 할 시스템이 서비스보다 빠르게 불어난다. 제이펍이 지난달 10일 펴낸 『그냥 Postgres를 쓰세요!』(데니스 마그다 지음, 윤명식 옮김)는 그 증식에 제동을 거는 책이다. 도발적인 제목에 대해 저자는 1장 첫머리에서 직접 해명한다.

"수십 년간 Postgres를 구축하고 사용해 온 전문가들이 건네는 합리적인 조언으로 받아들이시기 바랍니다."

이 문장을 기사의 첫 인용으로 고른 사람은 이원준 영풍문고 기술부문 MD다. "제목만 보면 만능론처럼 들리지만, 이 한 문장이 책 전체의 태도를 정한다"며 "새 요구가 생겼을 때 다른 데이터베이스부터 알아보지 말고 지금 가진 Postgres로 풀리는지 먼저 확인하라는 권유다. 부록 하나를 통째로 'Postgres를 사용하지 말아야 할 때'에 내준 것도 같은 맥락"이라고 말했다. 이어지는 문답은 영풍문고의 두 추천자가 이 책을 사이에 두고 나눈 이야기다.

Q. AI 서비스를 만드는 개발자가 데이터베이스 책을 읽어야 할 이유는.

권기원 영풍문고 서적팀 팀장은 3부를 짚었다. "확장 기능 생태계를 다루는 3부에서 pgvector로 생성 AI 기능을, TimescaleDB로 시계열을, PostGIS로 공간 데이터를, pgmq로 메시지 큐를 구현한다"며 "AI 서비스에 필요한 데이터 계층 대부분을 한 데이터베이스 안에서 시험해 볼 수 있다는 점이 가장 큰 쓸모"라고 답했다.

Q. 이미 Postgres를 운영하는 DB 실무자에게도 새로운 내용이 있나.

이 MD는 "기본기 장에서도 운영 감각이 묻어난다"며 "애플리케이션 계정에 최소 권한 원칙을 데이터베이스 수준에서 적용하라는 대목이나, 조건을 만족하는 행만 담는 부분 인덱스, 시계열 데이터에 맞는 BRIN 인덱스 설명은 바로 현업에 가져갈 수 있다. 워커 장애로 메시지가 처리 중 상태에 멈추는 문제를 다루는 메시지 큐 장도 실전적"이라고 말했다.

권 팀장은 "썬 마이크로시스템즈와 오라클에서 자바 플랫폼을 다루다 데이터베이스와 분산 시스템으로 옮겨 온 저자의 책을, 금융·게임·광고·클라우드 현장에서 25년 넘게 DB 엔지니어와 아키텍트로 일한 역자가 옮겼다"며 "추천사에 삼성SDS와 리눅스 재단 등 국내 데이터베이스 현업의 이름이 줄지어 오른 것도 그래서일 것"이라고 했다.

468쪽에 걸쳐 관계형 데이터베이스의 기본기에서 JSON과 전문 검색을 지나 AI와 시계열, 지리 공간까지 이어지는 이 책은 Postgres를 만능으로 포장하지 않는다. 강점과 한계를 함께 놓고 판단하게 한다는 점에서, 아키텍처 회의에 들고 갈 근거 자료로도 손색이 없다.

items.title: Tesla says customers can add their own vehicles to the robotaxi fleet next year — will it happen?
items.summary: For years, Elon Musk has been making big promises to Tesla owners about unsupervised autonomous driving and the ability to add their own vehicles to the company's robotaxi fleet. During today's third-quarter earnings call, the company finally gave itself a deadline. According to
items.content:
Tesla has set a Q2 2027 target to let owners opt their cars into its robotaxi network—a major promise, but one that comes with a history of missed deadlines and steep regulatory hurdles.

For years, Elon Musk has been making big promises to Tesla owners about unsupervised autonomous driving and the ability to add their own vehicles to the company’s robotaxi fleet . During today’s third-quarter earnings call, the company finally gave itself a deadline.

According to Tesla VP for Autonomous Driving Ashok Elluswamy, Tesla owners will be able to add their own vehicles to the company’s robotaxi fleet in the second quarter of 2027. Here’s his exact quote (emphasis ours):

Like I mentioned earlier, the software for Cybercabs and Model Y is the same. And pretty soon we’ll be able to release the same software as part of the V15 release to customers. The only additional requirement is to make sure that, for example, the customer Model Y can be part of the geofences and the fleet management that Tesla has for it to be fully autonomous. We suspect somewhere around Q2 next year is when we can turn on some of the first customer vehicles to be part of the robotaxi fleet.

It’s important to mark this deadline because it’s likely that Tesla will sail right past it. When it comes to autonomous driving and robotaxis, Musk has a pretty clear pattern: he sets bold, short-term deadlines that end up slipping by years — or never happening at all. Still, Tesla has made steady, incremental strides in the tech behind its consumer driver-assistance features. But the long-promised goal of “unsupervised” Full Self-Driving remains unfulfilled.

In 2019, Musk stood on stage at the company’s first AI Day and vowed that customer-owned vehicles could be used as part of a “Tesla Network” of robotaxis, earning their owners passive income while driving around autonomously, looking for fares. He likened it to Uber or Airbnb. Musk also said that by 2020, a “million” Tesla robotaxis would be out on the road.

As of yet, neither promise has come true. Tesla has a few hundred Robotaxis in Texas and Florida, some of which still have human safety monitors. It also has several dozen fully driverless Cybercabs in Austin.

Still, FSD growth was a bright spot in Tesla’s earnings this quarter. More people buying new Teslas in North America are choosing to add Full Self-Driving (Supervised), the company reported. Over 75 percent of new buyers picked the feature this quarter — a big jump of almost 20 percentage points compared to last quarter. Still, Tesla’s vehicle sales were down this quarter, as revenue flatlined and profits dipped.

Tesla also revealed a new Robotaxi safety website , in which the company says it has driven 3.3 million miles autonomously. That’s up from 380,000 unsupervised miles driven the company reported in July.

But even if Tesla opens up its robotaxi fleet to customer-owned vehicles, major regulatory hurdles remain. Unsupervised autonomous ride-hailing requires specific local and state regulatory permits. Insurance may be difficult to obtain. And in most places, it’s still illegal for individuals or outside companies to use their own self-driving cars as driverless taxis or passenger rides.

There’s also the tension between different types of Tesla owners. Older Model 3 and Y vehicles without the latest full-self-driving hardware suites (or AI compute infrastructure) are constrained by hardware capability. Dedicated vehicles like the Cybercab are built specifically for driverless passenger service, whereas consumer vehicles require additional software layers to guarantee safety without human intervention.

Tesla might be confident it can clear every technical and legal hurdle by Q2 2027. But history says this could easily become just another deadline that quietly slips by.

items.title: Blackstone’s Jas Khaira says fears over AI-buildout debt are overblown
items.summary: Blackstone’s AI head on why the PE giant isn't panicked by market jitters.
items.content:
Private equity giant Blackstone is putting itself at the center of the AI boom, firm veteran Jas Khaira discussed last week on stage at TechCrunch Disrupt.

It is writing checks via various strategies, ranging from offering massive loans to data centers to investing in frontier AI models and applications.

Earlier this year, the firm launched Blackstone N1 (BXN1), a San Francisco-based central hub for its AI initiatives. The group is led by Khaira, who relocated from New York to be at the epicenter of AI.

Unlike earlier tech cycles such as mobile or SaaS, which allowed companies to reach significant scale with moderate capital, the transition to AI requires staggering amounts of investment. That need for capital is precisely why Blackstone, with its $1.3 trillion in assets under management, could play such a critical role in this tech shift.

Khaira emphasized that Blackstone sets itself apart from traditional venture capitalists through its focus on compute financing and its ability to offer flexible capital structures, ranging from debt to equity. And it has been investing aggressively.

“We’re the largest owner of compute outside of the hyperscalers today, whether it’s investments in neo clouds, investments in data centers, and being able to use that compute strategically to support companies,” Khaira said.

For instance, BXN1 played a key role in several compute-related deals, among them Crux AI, a neocloud launched in partnership with Google to commercialize its custom TPUs, to which Blackstone committed $5 billion as an investor. It also backed four-year-old Etched , a chip startup whose rapid development has caught investor attention. Neoclouds are cloud providers that rent out AI GPU infrastructure.

Blackstone pioneered a financing structure that allowed it to lend massive sums to venture-backed cloud neoclouds by analyzing both committed customer contracts and using GPUs pledged as collateral.

Blackstone’s first such deal came in 2023 with CoreWeave, shortly after that neocloud saw demand explode following the launch of ChatGPT. Despite having only “30 million of revenue and minimal profitability” at that time, according to Khaira, CoreWeave approached Blackstone for a $2.3 billion loan.

CoreWeave was borrowing against the considerable value of its large collection of Nvidia GPUs, with Nvidia also an investor. Blackstone also grew more comfortable with the loan because CoreWeave had contracts with blue-chip customers like Microsoft.

That transaction quickly became the financing model for how Blackstone and other credit institutions provided billions in follow-on debt to CoreWeave and rival neoclouds.

“One of the primary things that we’re looking to is the nature of the customer. And if the customer is an investment-grade customer — let’s say it’s Microsoft or let’s say it’s Meta — the risk gets priced relative to that customer,” Khaira said.

Building on its success with CoreWeave, Blackstone struck other neocloud financing deals, including co-leading alongside Coatue a $10 billion credit facility for Australian GPU provider Firmus earlier this year.

Khaira acknowledged that in recent weeks, the large debt burdens accumulated by these companies and other neocloud operators have begun to raise red flags. Coreweave’s debt alone has since ballooned to about $50 billion , causing Altimeter Capital founder Brad Gerstner to note in a recent CNBC interview, “The collateral that CoreWeave is putting up which is really only GPUs is not good enough anymore. They used that in the past to get cheap debt.”

Khaira said that on the credit side, the market jitters stem from a combination of factors. Interest rates ticked up in September, and hotter-than-expected inflation signals that borrowing costs may keep climbing. The flood of AI infrastructure debt offerings isn’t helping either.

“We’re also seeing higher credit spreads,” Khaira said, explaining that lenders are charging higher premiums on top of already higher base interest rates to finance the AI buildout. “The cost of capital to price in debt for a Meta or a Microsoft has widened out,” he added, pointing out that even tech giants with massive balance sheets and solid earnings are paying more to borrow.

Concerns about the rising cost of debt have spilled into the stock market. Shares of CoreWeave dropped over 20% in recent days, while Firmus scrapped its planned IPO on the Australian Securities Exchange at a target valuation of roughly $30 billion.

“Ultimately, the market wasn’t there at that valuation, and so I think as a result, that deal didn’t get done,” Khaira said about Firmus’ cancelled listing.

“The market is thinking what is the right price for neoclouds, what is the right price for these businesses in this moment when interest rates are moving up,” he said.

Despite those pressures on some infrastructure providers, AI companies simply can’t get enough compute to power their models. Their appetite continues to drive data center buildout.

Khaira downplayed worries of doom-mongers that the massive accumulation of AI infrastructure debt could lead to a widespread credit crisis, or worse, crash the economy altogether. “This doesn’t feel like something where you’ve got 2008 banks that are shaky credits,” he said.

Instead, he pointed out that because the vast majority of data centers are built for hyperscalers, the debt financing them is ultimately backed “by the most creditworthy companies in the world.”

Beyond funding data centers, Blackstone is helping companies adopt AI through a $1.5 billion joint venture called “Ode with Anthropic,” formed alongside Anthropic and Hellman & Friedman this year. Ode supplies forward-deployed engineers to help companies adopt AI and integrate it into their operations, starting with Blackstone’s 280 portfolio companies.

items.title: Meta wants to pay for its broad AI buildout with a newly created class of stock
items.summary: The social media giant is planning a new stock strategy to help power its broad investments in AI models and services.
items.content:
Meta is making a big push into AI, and it’s creating a new kind of stock that could help pay for it.

On Wednesday, as the company reported its third-quarter earnings, Semafor reported the company might issue non-voting stock, meaning shares that don’t give their owners a vote on company decisions, to help fund its push into artificial intelligence.

During Meta’s earnings call, the company confirmed that reporting. Meta’s chief financial officer, Susan Li, said the company plans to “create a new class of non-voting capital stock, which will be distributed to all existing shareholders through a stock dividend.”

Li later added that the company “created this new class of shares with the purpose of creating a publicly traded non-voting stock usable for capital raising, employee compensation, acquisitions, and other general corporate purposes while preserving the voting power of existing Class A and B shareholders.”

The shares will allow the company to maintain its current “founder-led structure,” she added. They will also expand its “funding tools and give us flexibility to invest behind the unprecedented momentum we’re seeing across every part of our business, driven by AI.”

Meta’s earnings were strong this past quarter, beating Wall Street expectations. The company made $64 billion in revenue, a jump of 26% from a year earlier. Its costs and expenses also rose too, however, by 68% year over year.

Reality Labs, the division responsible for Meta’s AR glasses, VR headsets, and VR software, continues to lose money, though less than it used to. The company said in its earnings report that it expects the division’s losses to shrink from its 2025 levels to between $18 billion and $19 billion.

Meta has made a big push into AI over the past year. The company has released several AI models, including Muse Spark and Muse Glimmer earlier this year. In recent weeks, it added Muse Wonder and Muse Spark Open, an open-weight model whose underlying parameters are publicly available for outsiders to use and build on. Meta also launched a coding agent for software developers called Muse Code. At its Meta Connect event this year, the company announced a new line of cute and cuddly avatars for AI assistant, Meta Muse, in a push to make its AI services more relatable (and also meme-able ).

As far as can be discerned, those AI products are doing well. “In just a month and a half, more than 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada have set up Muse personal agents,” CEO Mark Zuckerberg said during Wednesday’s earnings call. “Growth continues to be strong, and we have been number one in the App Store almost every day.”

“Now that Muse has clear product-market fit, we are entering a new phase and a more operational phase that is focused on scaling it,” Zuckerberg added, claiming later that the company expects to grow the product’s appeal to eventually “serve billions of people.”

The company also noted that certain storm clouds linger on the horizon in the form of ongoing regulatory and legal issues. “We continue to monitor active legal and regulatory matters that could significantly impact our business and financial results,” said Li. “For example, we continue to see scrutiny on youth-related issues in several markets, and have a number of youth-related trials scheduled in the coming months in the United States.”

items.title: Mark Zuckerberg Agrees to Stay in California Despite Billionaires’ Tax Ballot Measure
items.summary: Meta’s board feared that its CEO’s departure could disrupt the company’s AI ambitions. A new stock agreement gives him financial incentives to stay put.
items.content:
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has agreed to keep living in Silicon Valley for eight years, potentially exposing himself to billions of dollars in one-time taxes if California voters approve a contentious ballot measure next month, according to a company regulatory filing released Wednesday.

During a dinner with Meta board members on September 9, Zuckerberg informed them that he was considering leaving California because of the measure, known as Proposition 40, and that he planned to list his Palo Alto, California home for sale four days later, the 109-page filing stated. The ballot proposal, which could be subject to lawsuits even if voters approve it, calls for a one-time 5 percent tax on stock and other assets held by billionaires in the state as of January 2026.

Many wealthy individuals, including Zuckerberg, currently avoid significant tax payments by borrowing against their shares and taking low salaries—$1 annually in the Meta CEO’s case. Zuckerberg purchased a home in Florida this past February, the Wall Street Journal reported at the time.

His potential cross-country move concerned a special committee of the board, whose members included attorney Robert Kimmitt, venture capitalist Charlie Songhurst, and DoorDash CEO Tony Xu. “The special committee was mindful about the difficulties the company faced during the COVID-19 pandemic when Zuckerberg could not be physically present with the company’s management team and did not want the company to face similar challenges going forward,” according to Wednesday’s filing.

Within days of the Meta board dinner, the special committee and Zuckerberg reached an agreement that links his ability to sell special company shares to his continued residence in California. It was finalized a week ago, and on Wednesday, Meta announced the details. It plans to create a new class of shares that hold no voting power. Selling these shares could potentially help raise funds for Meta’s expensive investments into AI data centers, without diluting Zuckerberg’s existing voting control.

All existing shareholders will receive the new nonvoting shares automatically in proportion to their existing holdings. Under what Meta called a “Founder Alignment Agreement” with Zuckerberg, he can sell 20 percent of those new shares to help pay any taxes he may owe. The remaining 80 percent would be available for sale in chunks over the next eight years as long as he remains in California. Any attempt to sell them early would require offloading some of his voting shares “unless there are material unforeseen circumstances that would render it prudent or advisable for Zuckerberg to reside elsewhere.”

Notably, the agreement specifies that Zuckerberg merely has to remain wherever Meta maintains its headquarters, so it’s possible that both he and the company could move together to another state. A number of California companies left for Texas , Nevada, and other states in recent years. Google cofounders Sergey Brin and Larry Page are among the handful of billionaires widely believed to have exited California over the potential tax.

But with much of the most pioneering AI development happening in Silicon Valley, leaving the city of Menlo Park could be a difficult proposition for the Meta board to stomach. “The goal is to keep Zuckerberg continuing to lead the company from California and in close proximity to Meta Superintelligence Labs,” the filing stated, referring to the company unit behind its recent Muse AI models .

In the end, the exercise may have been for naught. Recent polling in California suggests that with about $129 million spent campaigning against Prop 40, it will fail to muster enough votes.

items.title: Data centers could erase decades of air quality gains
items.summary: A rush of new data centers could bring air pollution roaring back to levels not seen since the 2000s in Texas, which has become ground zero for the physical infrastructure behind generative AI. New and proposed data centers are demanding a tremendous amount of electricity. How de
items.content:
New research out of Texas shows how data centers are driving up pollution.

A rush of new data centers could bring air pollution roaring back to levels not seen since the 2000s in Texas, which has become ground zero for the physical infrastructure behind generative AI.

New and proposed data centers are demanding a tremendous amount of electricity. How developers and utilities meet that demand — with gas turbines or renewable energy — will determine just how dirty things will get. So far, though, things are looking grim.

“There is a good chance that our children and grandchildren will breathe dirtier air than we did.”

In that scenario, fine particle pollution or soot from the power sector would more than triple, reaching its highest level since 2006. Smog-forming NOx emissions would increase 136 percent, approaching pollution levels from 2004. Planet-heating carbon dioxide pollution would climb 90 percent above what they were in 2025.

That’s not set in stone, of course. HARC modeled different outcomes based on three different projections for data center energy demand. Many proposed data center projects are speculative and could fall by the wayside. And developers can limit the environmental impact of a data center by building solar and wind farms onsite.

NOx emissions could be up to 10 times lower if data centers pair grid power with renewable electricity generated onsite. But if developers decide to build gas engines on site to power their data centers as a way to avoid long wait times to connect to the grid, the opposite could also play out, resulting in the highest pollution levels possible.

Data center capacity is typically measured by how much power they draw, and Texas has become the leading data center market in this measure with 26 gigawatts of existing and under-construction capacity. Texas is also bracing for four times more proposed data center capacity running on power generated onsite than any other state, according to a separate Wood Mackenzie report published in March. And in many cases, developers are turning to less efficient gas turbine technology in order to speed construction — another trend that’s making the data center boom more polluting than it needs to be.

“There is a good chance that our children and grandchildren will breathe dirtier air than we did,” John Hall, HARC CEO, said in a press release. “The transportation sector, the state, and other stakeholders have been working for decades to successfully bring these [emissions] numbers down, and that progress is now at risk.”

items.title: Airbnb limits chores for guests, sparking backlash from hosts
items.summary: Hosts are threatening to leave the platform after Airbnb says that they can no longer require guests to strip beds or do other time-consuming cleaning chores.
items.content:
Airbnb is taking steps to limit the chores that hosts can require of guests prior to checkout, addressing a long-standing grievance among customers who often pay cleaning fees and are told they must do a list of tasks themselves.

In a new policy update , Airbnb prohibits hosts from mandating that guests strip beds, wash and put away dishes, start laundry, or remove trash from the property. This new guideline will apply to reservations made on or after November 20.

This change comes in response to years of backlash regarding overly burdensome checkout instructions and hefty fines for not disposing of trash. Many guests have voiced their frustrations on social media, questioning why they should be responsible for cleaning tasks after already paying a cleaning fee.

However, some hosts aren’t pleased with the update. Within Airbnb’s community forums , some argue that basic cleaning responsibilities are essential for maintaining sanitary conditions and protecting their properties. They point out that hosts must manage the costs and practical demands of preparing their properties for the next guests.

One host expressed concern that the new policy leans towards a hotel-like model, which detracts from the unique appeal of Airbnb.

“Guests are given complete freedom to be lazy while the hosts bear the risk,” the host wrote. “The major distinction between commercial hotels and my private home is the personal touch. Guests can certainly be expected to wash their dishes or put them in the dishwasher and remove their dirty linens. In exchange, they enjoy a personal connection and a unique environment that a hotel simply can’t provide. Plus, every potential guest has the opportunity to read the listing beforehand and decide what they prefer. If these restrictions are removed, it could lead me to withdraw my listing and bid farewell to Airbnb after twelve years.”

Airbnb has outlined some exceptions to the new policy, though. Hosts may still ask guests to conserve water during droughts or use bear-proof trash containers in areas where wildlife poses a risk.

The policy change highlights the challenge Airbnb faces in balancing the expectations of guests versus hosts, and is another step taken in addressing guests’ concerns. The company faced scrutiny in 2024 over price transparency from hosts tacking on cleaning fees after guests booked their listings. In 2023, the company said more than 260,000 hosts had reduced or eliminated their cleaning fees. In May 2025, Airbnb began displaying total prices — including fees but excluding taxes — by default in search results worldwide.

It will be interesting to see how many hosts decide the new restrictions make Airbnb less attractive as a platform. But the move could also draw in more travelers who want the convenience of a rental without feeling as though they are both paying for housecleaning while still expected to clean the home themselves.

items.content:
지난주 AI 산업의 부채 문제가 불거지면서 세계 금융시장이 흔들렸습니다. 특히 AI 클라우드 업체 코어위브의 주가와 채권 가격이 급락하면서 AI 인프라 투자에 대한 경고가 쏟아졌습니다. 그런데 이 과정에서 눈길을 끈 인물은 코어위브 경영진이 아닌 젠슨 황 엔비디아 CEO였습니다.

그는 지난 15일(현지시간) 스웨덴 스톡홀름에서 코어위브의 재무 상태가 매일 개선되고 있다며 투자자들을 안심시켰습니다. 다음 날 독일 베를린에서도 AI 시장의 혼란에 대해 "이 모든 것은 지나갈 것"이라며 낙관적인 전망을 내놨습니다.

세계 최대 AI 반도체 기업의 CEO가 한 클라우드 업체의 재무 상태까지 직접 설명한 것은 눈길을 끄는 대목입니다. 그리고 그 이유는 엔비디아가 지난 몇 년간 네오클라우드라는 새로운 시장을 키워온 전략과 관련이 있습니다.

네오클라우드는 엔비디아의 GPU를 대량으로 확보해 AI 개발사나 기업에 컴퓨팅 자원을 빌려주는 업체입니다. 코어위브가 대표적입니다. 2017년 암호화폐 채굴 사업으로 출발한 코어위브는 2023년 생성 AI 열풍을 타고 GPU 클라우드 사업을 빠르게 키웠습니다.

이 과정에서 엔비디아는 최신 GPU를 공급하고 자금을 지원 하며 성장을 도왔습니다. 올해 1월에도 20억달러를 추가 투자했으며, 코어위브 지분 약 10%를 보유하고 있습니다. 2030년까지 5기가와트(GW) 규모의 AI 데이터센터를 구축하는 사업에도 협력하고 있습니다.

엔비디아가 코어위브를 이처럼 지원한 데에는 이유가 있습니다. 엔비디아는 AI 붐으로 막대한 돈을 벌어들였지만, 매출의 상당 부분을 MS와 아마존, 구글 등 소수의 대형 고객에게 의존 하고 있습니다.

문제는 이들이 엔비디아의 주요 고객인 동시에 잠재적인 경쟁자라는 점입니다. 엔비디아 GPU는 성능이 뛰어나지만, 가격도 비쌉니다. 따라서 자금력과 기술력을 갖춘 대형 클라우드 기업들은 자체 AI 칩을 개발하며 엔비디아에 대한 의존도를 낮추려고 합니다.

엔비디아로서는 장기적으로 GPU 판매를 유지하려면 이들 외에도 대규모 구매자를 확보할 필요가 있습니다. 네오클라우드가 바로 그런 역할을 합니다. 이들은 엔비디아 GPU를 사업의 핵심 자산으로 사용하며, 자체 AI 칩을 개발해 엔비디아와 경쟁할 가능성도 상대적으로 작습니다.

코어위브처럼 네오클라우드가 성장할수록 엔비디아는 대형 고객에 대한 의존도를 낮추고 새로운 GPU 수요를 확보할 수 있는 것입니다. 실제로 엔비디아의 지난 7월 분기 데이터센터 매출 중 대형 클라우드 기업을 제외한 고객의 비중은 45%에 달했습니다. 여기에는 네오클라우드뿐 아니라 일반 기업도 포함됩니다.

엔비디아가 지원한 업체도 코어위브뿐만이 아닙니다. 네비우스와 엔스케일 등 여러 네오클라우드 업체에 투자하거나 사업 구축을 지원해 왔습니다. 20일 등장한 분석 에 따르면 엔비디아가 데이터센터 사업을 지원하기 위해 제공한 보증과 컴퓨팅 용량 구매 약정 등은 지난 7월 분기 기준 최대 1645억달러에 달합니다. 이와 별도로 AI 클라우드 업체에 투자했거나 투자하기로 약속한 금액도 70억달러가 넘습니다. 직접 투자와 보증, 구매 약정 등을 합쳐 1700억달러 이상을 AI 인프라 시장에 걸어둔 셈입니다

그러나 이제 상황이 달라지고 있습니다. 디 인포메이션은 지난 18일 업계 경영진들을 인용해 현재 수백개에 달하는 네오클라우드 업체 중 몇 년 뒤에는 7~10개만 남을 수 있다는 전망을 전했습니다. GPU 확보와 데이터센터 건설에 막대한 돈이 들어가는 데다 경쟁까지 치열해지면서 상당수 업체가 독자적으로 살아남기 어렵다는 것입니다.

최근 코어위브 사태는 이런 위험을 보여준 사례입니다. 금융시장에서도 AI 기업들이 빚을 갚지 못할 가능성에 대비하는 거래가 급증했습니다. 파이낸셜타임스(FT) 에 따르면 주요 기술 기업의 채무불이행 위험에 대비하는 파생상품 거래 규모는 지난 7월 주간 20억달러 미만에서 9월에는 90억달러 이상으로 늘었습니다.

그렇다고 AI 컴퓨팅 수요 자체가 사라졌다는 뜻은 아닙니다. 코어위브 역시 당장 채무 상환 위기에 몰린 것은 아니며, 장기 계약을 바탕으로 사업을 운영하고 있습니다. 문제는 앞으로도 막대한 자금을 조달하며 사업을 키울 수 있느냐는 것입니다.

여기서 엔비디아의 고민이 시작됩니다. 네오클라우드 기업들이 잇달아 무너지면 공들여 키워온 GPU 판매처도 줄어들기 때문입니다. 특히 데이터센터를 직접 건설하는 업체들이 자금난으로 사업을 중단하면 GPU를 공급할 새로운 시설의 건설까지 차질을 빚을 수 있습니다.

월스트리트저널(WSJ) 은 20일 코어위브의 사업 모델이 흔들릴 때 엔비디아가 구제에 나설 강력한 경제적 이유가 있다고 분석했습니다. 다만 젠슨 황은 공식적으로 코어위브에 대한 추가 구제 지원이 필요하지 않다는 입장을 밝힌 바 있습니다.

그런 가운데 엔비디아가 이달 초 기업공개(IPO)를 철회한 호주 네오클라우드 업체 퍼머스 에 수억달러를 추가 투자하는 방안을 논의 중이라는 보도도 20일 나왔습니다.

이처럼 GPU 공급을 넘어 고객의 사업과 자금 조달까지 지원하고 있습니다. AI 산업의 '중앙은행' 이라는 비유도 나왔습니다. GPU를 판매하려면 이를 구매할 기업들이 필요하고, 그 기업들이 성장하려면 다시 엔비디아의 지원이 필요한 관계가 만들어진 셈입니다.

결국 코어위브 사태는 엔비디아에도 남의 일이 아닙니다. 네오클라우드 시장에 대규모 구조조정이 시작된다면 그동안 키워온 고객들을 어디까지 지원할 것인지 선택해야 할 수 있습니다. 젠슨 황이 지난주 직접 시장을 안심시키려 했던 이유도 이런 이해관계에서 찾을 수 있을 것입니다.

■ 앤트로픽, ‘숨은 의도 읽는’ 새 모델 준비...구글·오픈AI도 후속작 예고

구글과 오픈AI의 차세대 모델에 대한 소식이 잇따르는 가운데, 앤트로픽도 새로운 모델을 준비 중이라는 구체적인 정보가 나왔습니다. 특히 사용자가 명확하게 설명하지 않아도 숨은 의도와 목표를 파악하는 능력이 강조됐는데, 이는 과거 오픈AI를 비롯한 AI 기업들이 모델의 성능이 크게 도약할 때마다 내세웠던 특징이기도 합니다.

■ 엘리스그룹, AI 인프라 상장 랠리 가세...코어위브 악재 돌파할까

국내 AI 인프라 기업 엘리스그룹이 코스닥 상장 첫날 공모가보다 32% 하락하며 코어위브발 투자심리 악화의 영향을 받은 것으로 풀이됩니다. 래블업과 슈퍼브에이아이 등도 상장을 추진하고 있어 AI 인프라 기업에 대한 시장의 평가가 주목됩니다.

■ 머스크 “미국 모든 어린이에게 스페이스X 주식 1주씩”…14조원 규모

머스크가 앤트로픽의 회사 지분 5% 공익 기금 출연 발표에 대응해 내년 미국의 모든 어린이에게 스페이스X 주식을 1주씩 나눠주겠다고 약속했습니다. 약 14조원 규모로, 실제 이행된다면 수천만명의 어린이를 주주로 확보하면서 장기적으로 상당한 홍보 효과를 거둘 수도 있습니다.

items.title: Railway Security Disclosure
items.summary: Article URL: https://blog.railway.com/p/security-disclosure-wednesday-october-21st Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50188228 Points: 246 # Comments: 111
items.content:
Earlier this morning, Railway detected anomalous activity involving systems that store customer environment variables. After further investigation, our investigation to date indicates that an unauthorized third party may have accessed encrypted environment variables and, for some of them, obtained the decrypted contents. Environment variables may contain secrets such as API keys or database and registry credentials.

We believe this is part of a series of attacks recently targeting platform companies with the aim of compromising AI inference providers. We have notified these upstream providers to revoke all keys proactively, as we take these kinds of events extremely seriously.

While our initial analysis suggests the impact may be limited to a subset of users, we are nevertheless recommending that all users take the actions described below as a precaution to protect your systems while we complete our review.

What you should do: As such, we strongly recommend that you immediately roll all environment variables, including any API keys, stored in Railway, as well as any private registry credentials, and review logs for those services for unusual activity.

All deployments are paused while we investigate. Until builds are restored, you will not be able to roll out new versions. We apologize for this inconvenience. Follow this incident to be notified when builds resume.

As we confirm which accounts were affected, we will contact those customers directly by email with additional details.

We will provide new updates on this announcement, and on status.railway.com as we narrow the scope of impact.

items.title: Airbnb Hosts Are Furious They Can No Longer Make Guests Do Their Chores
items.summary: Some hosts are threatening to strike, while others are plotting ways around Airbnb’s new restrictions. Guests, meanwhile, are celebrating.
items.content:
Airbnb hosts are melting down over a new policy banning them from making guests complete tasks that “would typically be performed by a cleaner,” like “stripping the bed, taking trash offsite, or washing and putting away dishes.”

The change, which applies to all bookings made on or after November 20, quickly sparked outrage after it was announced in an email to Airbnb hosts on Wednesday. Many began fuming online about losing the right to make their guests clean up after themselves.

“As hosts, we have a responsibility to protect our investments, our homes, and, in many cases, our personal living spaces,” one person wrote in Airbnb’s official forum for hosts. “The problem is that Airbnb increasingly expects hosts to accept the risks while limiting our ability to protect ourselves.”

“Airbnb is like an abusive partner,” wrote one user on the Reddit community r/airbnb_hosts. “I'm alive long enough to recognize how truthful those few words are,” another person replied . “Until and unless I see substantive changes, I'm finally out.”

A different self-described host declared that going forward, the kitchens in their rentals will be “stripped down to only bare essentials.”

Many guests, meanwhile, are celebrating. For years, travelers have complained about having to pay hefty cleaning fees as part of their Airbnb bookings, only to be required to complete a list of chores before checking out.

“The guest experience has become total ass,” one person said in a subreddit for Airbnb hosts. “Clean dishes and run in the dishwasher. Strip the beds, put all linen in the laundry room. Take out all garbage, put in garbage can, take to the curb. Honestly, knock it off.”

Airbnb noted in its Wednesday announcement that hosts can’t get around the new policy by listing cleaning tasks in the “Requests” section of their listings instead. Airbnb spokesperson Simon Letouze tells WIRED that hosts can still make “reasonable” requests, such as asking guests to put dirty dishes in the sink. Other examples Airbnb cites includes asking guests to take short showers in areas with drought-related water restrictions, or telling them to place trash in bear-proof containers.

In a Facebook group for Airbnb hosts, one person posted what they claimed was a screenshot of their failed attempt to edit their property’s “Requests” section. They tried to ask guests to wash and air-dry dishes, put dirty towels in the laundry room, and take trash to a dumpster at an RV park they could find using a map on the refrigerator. But they realized they couldn’t hit save. Airbnb's interface had underlined and highlighted the requests in red and displayed a pop-up that read "Guests shouldn't be asked to do this task."

Hosts also can’t circumvent the new policy by giving guests a printed list of rules and asking them to sign it when they check in. On November 20, Airbnb is also banning hosts from requiring guests to sign separate contracts, with limited exceptions for local legal requirements, longer stays, or accessing “an optional amenity” like a “golf cart rental.”

If one of these situations applies, hosts have to mention it in the dedicated section of their listing. Airbnb adds that it “doesn’t help enforce the terms of these contracts.” Hosts who violate either policy, Airbnb warns, may receive warnings, or in severe situations, have their listings removed, or be banned from the platform entirely.

In a Facebook group for Airbnb hosts, one person posted a letter they claimed to have sent to company executives, demanding the ability to set their own “common-sense expectations” for guests. They encouraged others to send their own versions. Another asked if they should raise their prices, while a third called for hosts to organize a platform-wide strike.

“Even if we all unlist our properties for just a day or two, we can send a powerful message,” they wrote. “Airbnb built its empire on OUR properties. It’s time we reminded them who actually holds the power.”

Some hosts haven’t given up on finding a way to ignore or get around the changes. On Reddit, one person said they would simply move their rules to other sections of their listing, like “Guest Access.”(Airbnb did not immediately respond to WIRED’s inquiry about whether this would work.) Another person said they would give the guests a “house manual,” require the guest to read it, and provide a “codeword” as proof. (Several pointed out that this is not only unenforceable, but against current Airbnb policy.)

“First sentence of my requests section will now state ‘Here are my house rules!’" another person said , though it’s unclear whether Airbnb’s interface will allow this. They named “not smoking” as an example of one of their house rules, but Airbnb has said it enforces host-imposed smoking bans.

Unwanted smoking and other serious scenarios—like letting dirty dishes become “ health hazards ,” leaving “permanent stains on sheets,” and creating “mountains of rotting garbage" —were invoked by several hosts. But these policy adjustments, seemingly, will not change how any of these things are treated.

Airbnb already has its own ground rules that all guests must agree to. The general credo is to "treat your host’s home like your own," which translates to things like putting trash in the trash can, and not leaving moldy dishes.

If a host finds anything was damaged or went missing during a stay, guests are expected to pay a “reasonable” amount to repair or replace it. Hosts are also protected through the platform’s protection program, AirCover , which will reimburse up to $3 million for certain property damage caused by guests, including furniture, cars, and other belongings.

items.title: Enterprises keep buying software upgrades that IT thinks will make things worse
items.summary: Survey of 2,018 IT heads at big firms points to a lack of leverage.
items.content:
Enterprise-sized businesses spend, on average, 28 percent of their software budgets on unwanted upgrades, migrations, and licensing changes. Often, those firms’ IT heads think those changes are detrimental.

Those results are according to a survey of 2,018 chief information officers and senior IT decision-makers at companies with at least 10,000 employees that Origina commissioned for its report, “ The Software Tax .” About half of the respondents (1,011) are from the US, and the rest are from the United Kingdom. All respondents worked at companies with at least $1 billion in annual revenue.

Keep in mind that Origina provides maintenance for various enterprise software. Its report points to independent software maintenance as a way for IT leaders to regain control over software budgets, illustrating its potential bias. A third-party research consultancy, Censuswide , conducted the survey.

Among the report’s most concerning findings, enterprises often make software purchases that IT heads believe could hurt the organization. Ninety-five percent of respondents said “their organization has paid for a vendor-driven upgrade, migration, or licensing change in the past three years that it believed at the time would reduce performance, reliability, or business value,” the report says. Fifty-three percent of respondents “have done so more than once,” the report notes.

“Some 76 percent say their organization has very little real leverage in negotiations, and 80 percent say moving away from major vendors would cause significant disruption,” the report says, referring to the share of respondents who selected “strongly agree” or “somewhat agree” to those statements.

“When the alternative to an unwanted upgrade is losing support on systems the business runs on, saying yes is often a rational response,” Tomás O’Leary, one of the report’s authors and Origina’s CEO and founder, said in a statement. “That’s exactly the problem. The market has left some of the most experienced technology leaders in the world with little room to refuse, and that cost shows up in budgets, in engineering time, and in innovation that never gets funded.”

The result is less funding for other areas, particularly, per the report, innovation (named by 36 percent of respondents), human resources (32 percent), security (31 percent), and “customer-facing investment” (31 percent).

In a statement accompanying the survey’s announcement, Liberty Mutual’s CIO, James McGlennon, pointed out that an upgrade cycle could occupy top technical workers for “the better part of a year.”

“That’s not a one-off cost, it’s a recurring drag on capacity, and every year it repeats is a year those people aren’t working on the initiatives that actually differentiate the business,” he said.

The majority (91 percent) surveyed would support laws that give enterprises “protections comparable with those available to long-term residential tenants.” Only 1 percent opposed this (with the rest signaling that they neither support nor oppose the idea).

CIOs should “negotiate the exit before the entry” to have more control over software budgets, Marshall Van Alstyne, the report’s co-author and an information sciences professor at Boston University, said in a statement. Origina’s report suggests “settling the terms of a potential exit,” including setting a price for migration assistance and caps on renewal and expansion prices, during initial negotiations with the software vendor.

Origina’s report didn’t call out any specific vendors as forcing enterprises’ hands. However, every survey respondent currently runs “at least one of IBM, HCL, VMware/Broadcom, or SAP at meaningful scale.”

items.title: Tesla profits drop 43% in Q3
items.summary: Tesla’s once-booming energy storage business also shrunk in Q3 2026.
items.content:
Tesla published its third-quarter 2026 financial results this afternoon. Earlier in October, it reported its sales and deliveries for the three-month period, selling fewer cars than in the same quarter in 2025 , yet it still beat analyst projections. Now we can see how those sales translate to the bottom line. Tesla brought in $28 billion in revenue in Q3, almost the same as in 2025.

Automotive revenues were $20.6 billion, a 3 percent decrease year over year. Perhaps more troubling is the decline in revenue from solar panels and storage batteries—this line of business had been growing, but for Q3 revenue fell 16 percent year over year to $2.9 billion. Services and other revenues, though, which include parts and Supercharger use, grew by a third to $4.6 billion.

But the company—like the rest of us—has seen its expenses go up. Operating expenses rose by 39 percent to $4.8 billion, dropping the company’s operating margin to just 2.6 percent; in Q3 2025, Tesla’s margin was 5.8 percent. Net profit fell to $787 million, down 43 percent year over year. What’s more, capital expenditures were up by 110 percent to $4.7 billion, and free cash flow was down 62 percent to $1.5 billion.

Tesla can no longer rely on selling regulatory credits to other automakers: these fell to $113 million this quarter, down from $417 million in Q3 2025. Now, virtually every other automaker has a portfolio of electric vehicles and no longer needs to offset its emissions by pooling with Tesla. In the US, Tesla CEO Elon Musk’s support helped elect a president who has abolished such credits entirely, with Musk’s blessing .

Tesla’s letter to investors says its flat revenues were due to lower average selling prices, selling fewer cars, not receiving as much in credits, and also the decline of its energy storage business. Together with the reduced credits and battery and solar sales, a big jump in operating expenses is responsible for the diminishing profitability; some of this is Tesla spending rampantly on AI hardware, but some is also the CEO’s extravagant compensation package .

items.title: Meta to create a new class of shares to fund AI push
items.summary: Meta says it's issuing a new class of shares to fund its AI initiatives. As part of its third-quarter earnings report released on Wednesday, the company says the non-voting stock will also go toward potential acquisitions and employee compensation, with trading beginning in 2027.
items.content:
Meta says the new class of shares will also fund acquisitions and employee compensation.

Meta says it’s issuing a new class of shares to fund its AI initiatives. As part of its third-quarter earnings report released on Wednesday , the company says the non-voting stock will also go toward potential acquisitions and employee compensation, with trading beginning in 2027.

“The scale of investment required to compete, sustain growth, expand infrastructure, and pursue new strategic initiatives amidst the AI transformation taking place in the industry is significant,” Meta says in the press release. Susan Li, Meta’s chief financial officer, added during an earnings call that the new class of shares will “expand our funding tools and give us flexibility to invest behind the unprecedented momentum we’re seeing across every part of our business driven by AI.”

Meta has poured billions of dollars into the AI race as it builds ( and promotes ) sprawling data centers, poaches top talent from other companies like OpenAI, and builds AI models capable of rivaling those from other tech giants. The company expects capital expenditures between $135 billion and $145 billion this year, up from the previous $130 billion and $145 billion estimate.

It’s been a busy past few weeks for Meta, which launched its AI agent, Muse , in September. Like other AI agents, Muse can do things like clean out your email inbox, book restaurant reservations, and plan trips. The Muse app shot to the top of app stores shortly after its rollout, and hit 10 million downloads in the US this week. Meta also rolled out its Muse Wonder model this week .

Muse’s launch hasn’t come without some snags. Amid concerns about user privacy , a tech YouTuber reported that the agent gave out his address to a stranger on Facebook Marketplace. The company has also had to pause Muse’s conversation-sharing feature after researchers discovered chats publicly available on the web.

items.content:
오픈AI가 구글 클라우드를 통해 최신 AI 모델과 코딩 에이전트 ‘코덱스’를 판매한다. 챗GPT와 제미나이로 경쟁하는 두 회사가 기업 시장에서는 판매 협력에 나선 것이다. 오픈AI는 구글의 기업 고객에게 접근할 통로를 확보하고, 구글은 자사 모델뿐 아니라 경쟁사 모델을 원하는 고객까지 클라우드에 붙잡아 두겠다는 전략이다.

양사는 21일(현지시간) 공식 발표를 통해 오픈AI의 첨단 모델과 '코덱스'를 구글 클라우드의 AI 모델 제공 플랫폼 ‘모델 가든’에 도입한다고 밝혔다. 일부 기업 고객을 대상으로 비공개 프리뷰를 시작했으며, 몇주 내 정식 제공할 예정이다.

초기 제공 모델은 'GPT-6 아스트라'와 ‘GPT-6.1 솔’, ‘GPT-6 루나’다. 기업은 작업의 난도와 비용, 응답 속도에 맞춰 모델을 선택할 수 있다.

개발자는 코덱스의 명령줄 도구(CLI)와 데스크톱 앱을 구글 클라우드에 연결해 사용할 수 있으며, 향후 구글의 코딩 도구 ‘안티그래비티’와 기업용 AI 서비스에도 오픈AI 모델이 들어갈 예정이다.

사업적으로 중요한 부분은 결제 방식이다. 기업은 구글 클라우드 마켓플레이스에서 오픈AI 모델을 구매하고, 해당 사용료를 기존에 약정한 구글 클라우드 지출액에 포함할 수 있다. 구글에 일정 금액을 쓰기로 계약한 기업이 그 예산으로 오픈AI 모델까지 이용할 수 있다는 뜻이다.

사용료도 구글 클라우드 청구서에 통합된다. 오픈AI를 도입하기 위해 별도 공급사 계약과 구매 절차를 거쳐야 하는 부담을 줄이는 구조다.

보안과 데이터 관리도 기업 공략의 핵심이다. 양사는 구글 클라우드의 접근 권한 관리와 데이터 관리 체계를 오픈AI 모델 이용에 적용한다고 설명했다.

구글은 고객의 입력과 출력 데이터를 기반 모델 학습에 사용하지 않고, 고객이 모델 이용 기록을 기존 클라우드 환경에서 통합 관리·점검할 수 있도록 한다고 밝혔다. 금융과 의료 등 데이터 취급 규정이 엄격한 업종의 도입을 겨냥한 조치다.

오픈AI에는 마이크로소프트(MS) 중심이던 기업 판매망을 넓힌다는 의미가 있다. 이번 협력으로 오픈AI는 MS와 아마존웹서비스(AWS), 구글 클라우드 등 미국 3대 클라우드를 모두 판매 통로로 확보하게 됐다.

지난 4월 MS와의 독점 유통 관계가 해제된 뒤 AWS에 진출했고, 이번에 구글까지 합류했다. 기업이 쓰던 클라우드를 바꾸도록 설득하는 대신, 기업이 이미 사용하는 환경에 모델을 공급하게 됐다.

오픈AI는 이번 발표 말미에 MS가 여전히 자사의 주요 클라우드 파트너라고 명시했다.

구글에도 경쟁사 모델을 판매할 이유가 있다. 기업이 오픈AI 모델을 선택하더라도 구매와 이용을 구글 클라우드 안에서 처리하도록 만들 수 있기 때문이다.

구글은 기존 '제미나이'와 앤트로픽의 '클로드'에 오픈AI 모델까지 추가하면서, 주요 3개사의 폐쇄형 모델을 모두 제공하는 유일한 대형 클라우드라고 강조했다. 모델 선택권을 넓혀 고객이 다른 클라우드로 옮길 유인을 줄이려는 전략이다. 토머스 쿠리안 구글 클라우드 CEO는 오픈AI를 포함한 다양한 모델을 제공해 고객이 작업에 적합한 모델을 선택하도록 돕겠다고 설명했다.

두 회사의 협력은 이번이 처음은 아니다. 구글은 지난해 오픈AI에 컴퓨팅 자원을 공급하는 계약을 맺었다. 당시에는 오픈AI가 구글의 클라우드 고객이었다면, 이번에는 구글이 오픈AI 모델의 판매까지 맡게 됐다. AI 서비스와 검색에서는 경쟁하면서 컴퓨팅 자원 공급과 기업 영업에서는 협력하는 관계로 접점이 늘어난 셈이다.

다만 판매망 확보가 곧바로 모델 선택으로 이어지는 것은 아니다. 오픈AI는 같은 플랫폼에 입점한 제미나이 및 클로드와 성능과 가격을 놓고 경쟁해야 한다.

items.content:
4월·8월 요금 조정에 무선 ARPU 상승…루멘 광인터넷 인수 효과 반영

방송/통신 입력 :2026/10/22 06:15

미국 통신사 AT&T가 올해 두 차례 무선통신 요금을 인상한 가운데 3분기 매출이 전년 동기 대비 5.3% 증가했다. 기존 가입자에 대한 요금 조정과 광인터넷 사업 확장이 매출 성장을 뒷받침했다.

AT&T는 21일(현지시간) 3분기 매출 323억 달러, 조정 주당순이익(EPS) 0.65달러를 기록했다고 발표했다. 매출은 지난해 같은 기간 307억 달러보다 16억 달러 늘었고, 조정 주당순이익은 0.54달러에서 약 20% 증가했다.

AT&T는 지난 4월 일부 구형 무제한 요금제의 월 이용료를 인상한 데 이어 8월에도 일부 기존 요금제 가입자를 대상으로 요금을 조정했다.

이 같은 가격 조정과 가입자 증가에 힘입어 무선 서비스 매출은 전년 동기 대비 5% 늘었다. 후불제 휴대전화 가입자당 평균매출(ARPU)은 4% 상승했다.

광인터넷 사업에서는 루멘테크놀로지스의 일반 소비자 대상 광인터넷 사업 인수 효과가 반영됐다. 광인터넷과 고정무선접속(FWA)을 포함한 가정용 인터넷 서비스 매출은 전년 동기 대비 23% 이상 증가했다.

AT&T는 3분기 후불제 휴대전화 가입자 37만 9000명, 광인터넷 가입자 44만 2000명, FWA 가입자 32만 7000명을 각각 순증시켰다. 유무선 결합 고객 관계도 약 35만건 증가했다.

존 스탠키 AT&T 회장 겸 최고경영자(CEO)는 21일 실적발표 컨퍼런스콜에서 “우리 업계에서 가장 오래 유지되는 고객 관계는 광인터넷을 기반으로 우수한 무선 서비스를 함께 이용하는 고객”이라며 “이러한 고객이 가장 지속 가능하고 장기적인 고객 가치를 제공할 것”이라고 말했다.

루멘 인수로 확보된 광인터넷 기반 유선 가입자에 무선 요금을 결합해 판매하는 전략에 집중하겠다는 뜻이다.

매출 증가에도 영업이익은 41억 달러로 전년 동기 61억 달러보다 감소했다. 멕시코 무선사업 관련 손상차손과 인력 구조조정 비용 등이 반영됐다. 일회성 요인을 제외한 조정 영업이익은 76억 달러로 지난해 같은 기간 66억 달러보다 증가했다.

AT&T는 올해 조정 주당순이익 전망치를 기존 2.25~2.35달러에서 약 2.40달러로 상향했다. 연간 자본투자 규모는 230~240억 달러, 잉여현금흐름은 180억 달러 이상으로 예상했다.

items.title: Meta says Muse has over 10M users, with shopping a top activity
items.summary: Meta Muse users are adopting the app for shopping and personal productivity, the company said during Q3 earnings. The AI app now has over 10M users.
items.content:
Meta said during its third-quarter earnings call on Wednesday that its AI app Muse has been adopted by more than 10 million users, confirming estimates released earlier this week by market intelligence firm Sensor Tower.

But it is how people are using it, and how much they’re spending that has caught CEO Mark Zuckerberg’s attention. Zuckerberg said about 25% of people who set up Muse now use it daily, helping improve retention.

He also shared that over a quarter of Muse’s engaged users who were shopping via the AI agent, had an average purchase size of over $200, which was surprising even to industry insiders.

“Plaid told us that they hadn’t seen activity like they’re seeing with their connector on any other service before,” Zuckerberg said, referring to the financial technology company that connects payment apps to customers’ bank accounts. Muse uses Plaid’s connector to enable agentic shopping.

Beyond shopping, Zuckerberg said other popular uses for Muse include personal productivity tasks, such as connecting the AI agent to users’ email or calendars. The exec stressed that this indicates users trusted Muse’s security setup, which includes a feature called “Muse Secure VM” designed to protect their data and privacy. He also mentioned that the forthcoming “Muse Confidential VM” will prevent even Meta from seeing users’ content.

Now that Muse has achieved “product-market fit,” Zuckerberg said Meta’s focus will shift to scaling the AI agent, increasing revenue, and optimizing its compute costs. Remarkably, the tech company is forecasting that Muse will eventually bring in more revenue per user than its “family of apps” users do today — meaning its users on Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Messenger. Currently, that figure is around “several hundreds of dollars annually,” Zuckerberg said.

Meta has said it ultimately intends to monetize Muse by keeping it free for most users, but keeping a percentage of the commerce taking place on the platform. Power users who want access to the most advanced AI models or more tokens will also have to pay.

Zuckerberg also noted that Meta believes Muse will be profitable after it scales.

“On the compute side, we are building out the capacity to serve more than a billion people over the next few years,” he told bankers and analysts on the Q3 earnings call. “In the near term, Muse is very compute-intensive to run, but we expect to improve its cost efficiency by more than 10x in the next year, which will enable it to be profitable once the revenue lines are at scale.”

Muse will also play a central role in Meta’s smart glasses strategy. Reality Labs, the division responsible for smart glasses, VR, and the metaverse, is still losing billions. However, the division’s losses are expected to improve from $19.1 billion in 2025 to $15 billion this year.

Beyond scaling and supporting its hardware strategy, Zuckerberg teased the company’s plans for something he called the “Muse network.” He described this as taking Muse from a “single-player game” to one where “your Muses can work with your friends’ and your families’ [Muses].”

“And if you want to buy something, it’s not just navigating to that business’s website; it’s talking to their agent,” he added.

items.title: Year-old AI lab Flapping Airplanes raises $1B at a $6B valuation
items.summary: Just 9 months after raising an $180 million seed round, Flapping Airplanes has landed $1 billion Series A for its mission to build AI models "without ingesting half the internet."
items.content:
Year-old startup Flapping Airplanes has wowed Silicon Valley with an impressive founding team and a mission to find ways to train large models with less data. On Wednesday, the company announced it had raised a $1 billion Series A round, co-led by Index and Lux, reportedly at a $6 billion valuation.

The round comes just nine months after the company launched with a $180 million seed round from GV, Sequoia, and Index. That seed round had valued the company at $1.5 billion, so its valuation just quadrupled.

Other participants in the new round included earlier backers Sequoia, GV and Kleiner Perkins. Valor, Atreides, Kleiner Perkins, A*, and Nvidia are also investors in the company.

Flapping Airplanes was founded by Aidan Smith and brothers Asher and Ben Spector. Smith is a former founder and Thiel fellow who worked at the brain implant company Neuralink during college. Asher Spector was a statistics PhD at Stanford, while Ben Spector was a computer science PhD student at Stanford and founded Prod while at MIT.

Prod is an almost secret-society, five-year-old student-run startup accelerator that has “become one of the most powerful talent incubators in Silicon Valley,” wrote Sequoia partner David Cahn , a Flapping Planes investor, in a post earlier this year explaining why he invested. Together, the founders “are building the ‘young person’s AGI lab,’” as Cahn described it.

The founders describe their work as “the world’s most complete megakernel framework. It can perform entire training runs, serve inference, play video games, and even do all three simultaneously in a single kernel.” (A kernel is a program that runs on a GPU, and a megakernel bundles many tasks into one program.)

The founders claim the framework “can overlap memory-bound inference with compute-bound training,” meaning it can run a task that spends most of its time waiting for data to be fetched alongside one that spends most of its time doing math, so the chip is rarely sitting idle. The premise is that AI has barely scratched the surface of what GPUs can do, and they believe it can create intelligent systems “without ingesting half the internet.”

The goal is systems that cost less to train and run. “A model that’s a million times more data efficient is probably a million times easier to put into the economy,” Asher Spector told TechCrunch shortly after the startup launched.

They now have a fresh $1 billion to hire and attempt to turn that goal into reality.

인도 최대 이동통신사를 거느린 지오플랫폼이 기업공개(IPO) 첫날 약 100분 만에 전체 공모 물량에 해당하는 청약을 확보했다.

기관투자자 청약 경쟁률은 9배를 넘었지만 개인투자자 청약은 배정 물량에 미치지 못해 투자자 유형별 수요 차이가 뚜렷하게 나타났다.

21일(현지시간) 로이터통신 등에 따르면 지오플랫폼은 청약 개시 100분 만에 전체 공모 물량을 채웠다. 기관투자자 배정 물량은 접수 시작 10분 만에 소화됐다.

당일 오후 5시 기준 전체 청약 경쟁률이 3배를 넘었다. 적격기관투자자(QIB) 청약 경쟁률은 9배를 웃돈 반면, 개인투자자 청약은 배정 물량의 약 70%에도 미치지 못했다. 청약은 23일까지 이어진다.

지오플랫폼의 공모 규모는 최대 3021억 3000만 루피(약 4조 5000억원)로 인도 증시 사상 최대다.

기존 기록은 2024년 현대자동차 인도법인이 세운 약 2780억 루피다.

공모에서는 신주 2억 7000만주를 주당 1065~1119루피에 발행한다. 공모가 상단을 적용한 기업가치는 약 1083억 달러로 평가된다.

청약에 앞서 진행된 기관투자자 대상 앵커 배정에서도 높은 수요가 확인됐다. 지오플랫폼은 19일 212개 투자자에게 약 811억 루피 규모의 주식을 배정했다.

블랙록, 피델리티, 싱가포르 국부펀드 GIC, 아부다비투자청 등이 참여했으며 앵커 투자 신청액은 배정 규모의 30배를 넘은 것으로 전해졌다.

IPO는 기존 주주가 보유 주식을 매각하는 구주매출이 아닌 신주 발행 방식으로 진행된다. 따라서 공모 자금은 기존 주주가 아닌 지오플랫폼에 유입된다.

회사는 공모 순조달금 가운데 2750억 루피를 통신 자회사 릴라이언스지오인포컴의 차입금 조기 상환에 사용할 계획이다. 나머지는 일반 기업 운영 등에 투입한다. 신주 발행을 통한 재무구조 개선이 이번 IPO의 주요 목적이라는 의미다.

국제 신용평가사 무디스는 이번 IPO가 통신 자회사의 부채와 이자 부담을 줄이고 모회사 릴라이언스인더스트리의 자금 운용 여력을 높일 수 있다는 점에서 신용도에 긍정적이라고 평가했다.

지오플랫폼은 오는 23일 청약을 마감하고 28일 인도 봄베이증권거래소(BSE)와 국립증권거래소(NSE) 상장을 추진한다.

items.title: 웹사이트 70% 쓰는 PHP서 AI가 결함 발견…각국 정부 사이트 중단

items.content:
AI가 웹사이트 구동에 널리 쓰이는 프로그래밍 언어 PHP에서 중대 보안 취약점을 찾아내면서 유럽 정부와 병원, 학교 등이 웹사이트를 잇달아 중단했다. 공격자가 서버를 장악할 수 있는 결함이 확인되자 피해를 막기 위해 접속부터 차단한 것이다. 긴급 수정본은 배포됐지만, 공격자 역시 AI로 이를 분석해 업데이트하지 않은 서버를 노릴 수 있어 대응 속도가 중요해졌다.

로이터와 블룸버그 등은 21일(현지시간) PHP에서 두 가지 심각한 취약점이 공개된 뒤 유럽 각국 정부와 기관들이 긴급 업데이트와 서비스 중단에 나섰다고 보도했다. 미국 정부도 연방기관과 주요 기반 시설을 보호하기 위해 기술 기업들과 보안 패치 적용을 지원하고 있다.

네덜란드에서는 정부 포털과 로테르담 항만, 축구협회, 주요 정당과 여러 병원의 대외 공개 웹사이트가 중단됐다. 현지 통신사 ANP에 따르면 소프트웨어업체 노투비즈의 서비스를 이용하는 지방자치단체와 주 정부, 물 관리기관 등 100곳 이상도 영향을 받았다.

덴마크에서는 학교 소통 플랫폼 등이 멈췄고, 핀란드와 독일, 프랑스도 정부 웹사이트를 일시 차단했다. 독일 프라이부르크대와 오스트리아 빈대, 위키미디어 재단과 인터넷 아카이브도 일부 사이트나 시스템을 중단했다.

이들 기관이 모두 해킹당한 것은 아니다. 독일과 핀란드는 예방 조치라고 설명했으며, 핀란드는 취약점 악용 시도나 데이터 유출 때문에 서비스를 중단한 것은 아니라고 밝혔다.

PHP는 웹사이트 서버에서 이용자의 요청을 처리하고 화면에 표시할 내용을 만드는 프로그래밍 언어다. 무료 오픈소스로 제공되며, 워드프레스와 드루팔, 줌라 등 웹사이트 제작·관리 도구의 기반으로 쓰인다.

서버 측 프로그래밍 언어를 확인할 수 있는 웹사이트의 약 70%가 PHP를 사용한다. 전체 웹사이트의 약 40%를 구동하는 워드프레스도 PHP에 의존한다. 여러 서비스가 함께 쓰는 기반 기술에서 결함이 발견돼 영향이 커진 것이다.

‘PHP2Shell’로 불리는 두 취약점은 특정 조건에서 계정이나 비밀번호 없이 서버에 명령을 실행할 수 있는 결함이다. 심각도는 각각 10점 만점에 9.2점으로 평가됐다. 공격에 성공하면 데이터를 훔치거나 웹페이지를 변조하고 시스템을 장악할 수 있다.

이번 발견에는 오픈AI와 구글의 AI 모델이 활용됐다. 보안업체 캘리프(Calif)는 ‘GPT-5.6 솔’을 활용해 취약점을 찾아 지난 8월 신고했다. 알파벳 산하 보안업체 위즈(Wiz)도 자체 AI 도구와 구글의 ‘제미나이 4 아르곤’, GPT-5.6 솔을 활용해 독립적으로 문제를 확인했다.

위즈에 따르면 결함은 10년 이상 PHP 코드에 남아 있었지만, 실제 공격으로 연결하는 과정이 매우 복잡했다. AI가 이 장벽을 낮췄다는 설명이다. 위즈는 “세계적인 연구팀이 몇 달에 걸쳐 수행했을 작업을 연구원 한 명이 일주일 만에 완료했다”고 밝혔다.

개발진은 문제의 징후를 알고도 수정을 마치지 못했다. PHP 재단은 2024년 취약점 하나의 징후를 발견했지만 구체적인 공격 경로를 확인하지 못했고, 수정 방식도 결정하지 못했다고 설명했다. 재단은 의사결정 과정과 자원 부족에 따른 “구조적 실패”라고 인정했다.

PHP 개발진은 취약점 관련 정보와 공격 시연 영상이 예정에 앞서 공개되자 배포일을 하루 당겨 21일 수정본을 내놨다. 그러나 수정본 공개는 공격자에게도 결함을 분석할 단서를 제공한다. 보안업체 TLP:블랙의 코스틴 라이우 공동창업자는 AI가 취약점 “악용 경쟁”을 부추기고 있다며 대규모 공격 가능성을 경고했다.

클라우드플레어는 이미 일부 초기 공격 시도를 관찰하고 고객 보호 조치를 도입했다고 밝혔다. 미국 사이버보안·인프라보안국(CISA)은 발표 시점까지 악용 사례를 확인하지 못했다고 전했다. 다만 실제 침입이나 데이터 유출 등 피해 규모는 아직 확인되지 않았다.

당장 필요한 조치는 PHP 사용 여부를 확인하고 서버에 수정본을 적용하는 것이다. 워드프레스의 일반적인 자동 업데이트만으로는 해결되지 않으며, 서버에 설치된 PHP 자체를 업데이트해야 한다.

미국 국가안보국(NSA)과 유럽 보안기관들은 즉시 업데이트하기 어렵다면 수정과 검증을 마칠 때까지 해당 시스템의 외부 접속을 차단하라고 권고했다. 영국 국가사이버보안센터(NCSC)는 이미 침입한 흔적이 있는지도 검사하라고 안내했다.

오래된 서버는 대응에 시간이 걸릴 수 있다. 인터넷 분석업체 센시스에 따르면 관측한 약 260만개 호스트 가운데 150만개가 수정본을 제공받기 어려운 PHP 버전을 사용하고 있었다.

공식 지원이 끝난 버전은 지원 중인 버전으로 전환하거나 공급업체의 별도 지원을 확인해야 한다. 수정본이 배포됐더라도 개별 서버에 적용되기 전까지는 공격 위험이 남는다.

items.summary: Meta had to shell out $9.89 billion to pay for a chunk of the child safety settlement it reached with US attorneys general. That's according to the company's third-quarter earnings report released on Wednesday, which says Meta's income from operations would have been $22.89 billi
items.content:
Meta’s third-quarter earnings report shows it spent $9.89 billion paying for its settlement with US attorney generals.

Meta had to shell out $9.89 billion to pay for a chunk of the child safety settlement it reached with US attorneys general. That’s according to the company’s third-quarter earnings report released on Wednesday , which says Meta’s income from operations would have been $22.89 billion without the settlement.

In August, Meta agreed to pay $17.1 billion to settle a massive nationwide lawsuit that claimed the company harmed children by making its social media platforms “addictive” by design. It will also only pay $5.3 billion of this amount if YouTube and TikTok implement stricter settings and safeguards for kids, which Meta also agreed to as part of the settlement.

Meta’s total costs and expenses amounted to $51.61 billion, including the amount it agreed to pay as part of the settlement. The company may have even bigger litigation costs in its future, as a New Mexico court ordered Meta to pay $25 billion over the Cambridge Analytica scandal on Wednesday.

Even with the fees associated with its legal battles, Meta reported earning $64.60 billion in revenue, marking a 26 percent increase from the same time last year. “We hit major milestones this quarter toward delivering personal superintelligence for everyone,” Meta CEO Zuckerberg says in the press release. “Our investments are paying off, the core business is strong, and we’re seeing velocity across the board.”

글로벌 OTT와 미디어 업계 전문가들이 서울에 모여 스트리밍 시장의 변화와 콘텐츠 수익화 전략을 논의한다. 광고 기반 무료 스트리밍부터 팬덤 비즈니스, 콘텐츠 지식재산권(IP) 확장, AI 기술 활용까지 다양한 산업 현안을 다룰 예정이다.

방송미디어통신위원회는 한국방송광고진흥공사와 함께 오는 11월5일 서울 광화문 포시즌스 호텔에서 '2026 국제 OTT 포럼'을 개최한다.

올해로 5주년을 맞은 포럼에서는 글로벌 광고 기반 무료 스트리밍 플랫폼 투비(Tubi)의 데이비드 살몬 부사장이 기조연설을 맡는다. 팬덤과 시청자 취향에 기반한 콘텐츠 추천, 크리에이터 협업 등을 중심으로 글로벌 스트리밍 산업의 발전 방향을 제시한다.

이어 중국 소셜미디어 플랫폼 샤오홍슈의 성샹 마케팅 연구소장과 서황욱 구글코리아 유튜브 한국·중화권 총괄이 광고와 커머스를 결합한 플랫폼 수익화 모델을 소개한다.

국내 OTT 해외 진출 전략도 주요 의제다. 강유진 티빙 전략총괄헤드는 특별세션에서 지난 5년간 국내 OTT 산업의 성과를 돌아보고 향후 글로벌 시장 확대를 위한 전략을 발표한다.

콘텐츠 IP 확장 전략을 다루는 토크콘서트에는 유튜브 예능 '핑계고'의 조은진 PD와 '뿅뿅 지구오락실'의 박현용 PD가 참여한다. 노가영 작가의 진행으로 콘텐츠를 활용한 사업 다각화와 팬덤 구축 경험을 공유한다.

영국 BBC의 케렌사 사마니디스 iPlayer 총괄과 김진만 MBC 제작본부장은 지상파 방송과 OTT를 연계한 디지털 전환 사례를 발표한다. 임주영 웨스트월드 기술연구소장은 AI 도입에 따른 시각특수효과(VFX) 제작 환경의 변화를 소개한다.

행사장에는 티빙, 웨이브, 에그이즈커밍의 홍보부스와 참관객 참여 행사도 마련된다.

items.summary: Two bugs found with AI are behind major issues today for 4chan, DeviantArt, Wikipedia, and the blog where the bar around the corner posts pictures of people's dogs. The "critical vulnerabilities" were discovered in the PHP programming language, which underpins much of the interne

Two bugs found with AI are behind major issues today for 4chan, DeviantArt, Wikipedia , and the blog where the bar around the corner posts pictures of people’s dogs. The “critical vulnerabilities” were discovered in the PHP programming language, which underpins much of the internet, including any site built on WordPress. But it’s far bigger than that. Some Dutch and Finnish government agencies took their sites down as a precaution. The NSA Cybersecurity account on X recommended that organizations take their systems offline if “an immediate update is not feasible,” as did the UK’s National Cyber Security Center . Even Pokémon Home and Pokémon Champions were taken offline, Kotaku reports .

The vulnerability isn’t exactly new. It’s been present in PHP for roughly 20 years, but exploiting it “required an exceptionally complex chain of steps, at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve,” according to security firm Wiz . However, powerful AI models have made it much easier to turn that kind of obscure bug into dangerous vulnerabilities.

As a casual internet user, you might be wondering what exactly the barrage of jargon like “RCE via OOM corruption” means, how concerned you should be, and how exactly a vulnerability this severe flew under the radar for so long.

W3Techs, a survey service, says that the PHP programming language is used by “69.3 percent of all the websites whose server-side programming language we know,” including popular sites like Wikipedia and WordPress. The internet security site VirusTotal says its scanner currently registers about 3.8 million sites running PHP with at least one port open.

According to OpenAI , an AI security group called Calif identified a “critical” PHP flaw using GPT-5.6 Sol, and Google-owned Wiz independently discovered and reported the vulnerabilities using AI. The PHP Foundation says that an exploit for one of the vulnerabilities “was theorized” in 2024, but “no concrete vectors were found and other concrete issues with clear impact overshadowed these concerns.”

Now the PHP Group says hackers could use the two vulnerabilities for “unauthenticated remote code execution,” like running their own code, changing content, and accessing a site’s stored data without needing an administrator login or password.

RCE via OOM corruption, CVE-2026-109618 ( GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w ): out-of-memory handling can interrupt PHP while internal request data is only partially initialized. Request cleanup may then treat the invalid data as valid.

RCE via stale global state, CVE-2026-109619 ( GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp ): request-owned internal state can survive after its backing memory has been freed. A later request handled by the same worker may use that stale state before normal initialization resets it.

Very. The PHP Group says that basically any site running PHP is at risk. OpenAI, which was involved in the vulnerability research, said: “We consider this one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory.” And Wiz said it’s “among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered … in software history.”

Last night, the CTO of Cloudflare said that it was “seeing early attacks emerging.”

It’s hard to understate just how bad this could get. The vulnerabilities could allow an attacker to take full control of a server. That includes gaining access to passwords, API keys, cryptographic certificates, and databases of sensitive information. They could also execute code on those servers, turning them into vectors to attack other vulnerable servers. And, thanks to AI, it’s relatively trivial for a determined hacker to exploit these flaws now that they have been revealed.

As a user, not much. The vulnerability affects servers running PHP and doesn’t necessarily target users directly, but it could use compromised sites to spread malware and steal other valuable data. If you’re feeling extra cautious, check the social accounts of sites and services you frequently use to see if they’ve posted any updates before visiting.

If you have a website, even a simple blog, it’s time to check what version of PHP your site uses, if any. If you’re using a service like Squarespace or Wix, you’re in the clear, as those don’t support PHP.

Customers of Hostinger, GoDaddy, Bluehost, or other web hosting services should be more cautious. GoDaddy says that any site using PHP should assume it is affected and update to the fixed release as soon as possible. It also says that sites running PHP 8.1 or older should upgrade to a newer version, as they’re no longer supported and there will not be an official fix coming.

Those on a managed hosting service should check with their provider to see when they should expect the fix to be deployed. If you sell products or services or have any sensitive data on your servers at all, it’s best to disable your site until your host patches their version of PHP.

items.title: Tesla starts Optimus robot production in California as profit falls 43%
items.summary: Tesla's revenue was flat and its expenses skyrocketed as it pressed the accelerator on its Optimus robots, AI, and autonomous driving.
items.content:
Tesla has started production of its Optimus humanoid robot at its factory in Fremont, California, a manufacturing space once dedicated to making electric vehicles, the company announced Wednesday.

“The bots coming off this line are the first production-quality bots that we have manufactured,” Tesla wrote in its third-quarter letter to shareholders. “While we will continue to iterate on the hardware and manufacturing process, we have proven that the current manufacturing process for Optimus is suitable for a commercial product.”

That fordward-looking development wasn’t enough to lift the company’s otherwise middling third-quarter earnings, results that typify a company at the midpoint of a major bet. Tesla’s revenue was flat and its expenses skyrocketed as it pressed the accelerator on its Optimus robots, AI, and autonomous driving. The end result was a 43% drop in profits.

The company’s revenue was largely driven by EV sales, which were flat year-over-year at $20 billion. Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles in the third quarter, about 6,000 more than the previous quarter, but fewer than in the same period last year.

Tesla’s total third-quarter revenue was $28.04 billion, a skosh below the $28.09 billion it generated in the third quarter of 2025. Tesla’s third-quarter revenue was also about $200 million lower than the previous quarter’s haul of $28.23 billion.

Tesla saw a 16% year-over-year drop in its solar and energy storage business to $2.8 billion, which it blamed on tariff-related customer refunds. There was some positive revenue growth in its services business, a category that includes customer subscriptions to its Full Self-Driving advanced driver-assistance software. Tesla’s services business grew 33% year-over-year, bringing in $4.6 billion.

None of this was enough to outpace Tesla’s spending on artificial intelligence projects and its Optimus robot, which took a big bite out of profits.

The company reported $787 million in net income, a 43% drop from the same period in 2025 when it earned $1.37 billion. Lower regulatory credit sales also put pressure on its profitability. The company stayed in the black in large part because of a big boost from its “services and other” segment, which accounted for a record $734 million in gross profit for the quarter.

items.title: Recursive launches Flint, a laptop coding model it says was largely built by AI
items.summary: Startup Recursive has released Flint, a free, laptop-sized coding model built largely by its own AI research system, as an early test of AI that improves itself.
items.content:
Recursive , an AI startup founded last year, is starting to live up to its name. The company, which is trying to build AI that can improve itself, released its first model, Flint , on Wednesday. Flint is a free coding model that can run on a laptop and was built largely with the help of AI.

Recursive’s automated research system, which it calls the Eureka Machine, helped with nearly every step of Flint’s development, the company says. That let a small team build the model from scratch in under four months.

Flint is an early public test of recursive self-improvement: the idea that AI can build better AI, which in turn builds even better AI. It’s also one of the most debated ideas in the industry. Some researchers fear that AI improving itself could slip out of human control. For now, Recursive’s version is more limited: an AI research assistant overseen by people that produced a model small enough for a laptop.

The company emerged from stealth in May with $650 million in funding at a $4.65 billion valuation, from backers including GV, Nvidia, and AMD Ventures. Recursive is led by CEO Richard Socher, Salesforce’s former chief scientist.

Because Flint runs on a user’s own computer rather than a company’s cloud servers, developers can use it offline, keep their code private, and avoid the usage fees that AI cloud services charge based on how much text the model processes. The model is free to download on Hugging Face, the popular site for sharing AI models, under the Apache 2.0 license, an open-source license that allows free use and modification.

Flint is a mixture-of-experts model, meaning it uses only a small slice of itself for any given task: just 2.5 billion of its 40 billion settings, known as parameters, at a time. That makes it light enough for an ordinary laptop and far smaller than Meta’s Muse Spark Open , an open model built for Macs that was released last week. Muse Spark Open uses 816 billion parameters and needs at least a terabyte of memory.

Flint is also fast. In Recursive’s tests, it generated about 131 tokens (chunks of text) per second on a MacBook Pro with Apple’s M4 Pro chip — roughly twice the 58 to 69 tokens per second that similar models managed on the same machine, including Google’s Gemma 4 and Nvidia’s Nemotron 3.5 Lightning. On Nvidia’s RTX Spark, Flint topped 150 tokens per second.

On SWE-Bench Verified, a benchmark that measures how well AI can fix real-world software bugs, Flint outperformed other models under 50 billion parameters. On Recursive’s own average across six tests, only one model, Alibaba’s Qwen3.8 27B, scored higher than Flint.

The company acknowledged that Flint would need more guidance than the big paid coding assistants, and suggested breaking large tasks into smaller steps. Still, early reviews were positive. Wired’s Will Knight used Flint on a Mac with 48GB of memory to build several small programs, including a to-do list app and a tool that scours the web for research. He found that smaller coding models often ran into errors or were slow compared to Claude or Codex, but Flint nailed his coding requests every time.

The Eureka Machine comes up with ideas, runs experiments and uses the results to decide what to try next. According to the company’s launch video , it contributed to nearly every part of building Flint, from pre-training to post-training and inference.

Recursive said that Eureka’s contributions include a sparser model shape, low-bit training that shrank Flint by 71% with almost no loss in quality and custom kernels, which are specialized programs that speed up the underlying computations.

Recursive didn’t say how much time the Eureka Machine saved its researchers, but it’s not alone in leaning on AI to do research. OpenAI said last month that by mid-August, its AI agents were logging 3.1 workdays for every one worked by a human researcher.

If Recursive’s bet pays off, each new model should be able to take on longer stretches of work without human help. The company previously told TechCrunch that its $410 million compute deal with Amazon Web Services in June was “less about headcount and more about agent count.”

The longer-term goal, Socher told Wired, is for the Eureka Machine to achieve full recursive self-improvement, with humans overseeing the process and able to stop it if something goes wrong. Recursive says each new model should make the Eureka Machine a better researcher, helping it build the next one faster.

items.title: Flying Roadsters can’t lift Tesla’s flat Q3 revenues
items.summary: As the smoke clears from its outrageous Roadster demo, Tesla reported Q3 earnings on Wednesday - and the cold reality is that revenue has flatlined. Tesla said it earned $1.7 billion in net income on $28.0 billion in revenue in the quarter that ended in September 2026. Revenues w
items.content:
Flat revenue and a 4 percent profit drop show that no amount of rocket thrusters can disguise Tesla’s troubles.

As the smoke clears from its outrageous Roadster demo , Tesla reported Q3 earnings on Wednesday — and the cold reality is that revenue has flatlined.

Tesla said it earned $1.7 billion in net income on $28.0 billion in revenue in the quarter that ended in September 2026. Revenues were flat, while profits dropped 4 percent compared to the third quarter of 2025 , when the company earned $1.4 billion in net income on $28.1 billion in revenue. Tesla’s revenue came in above Wall Street expectations of $27.9 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG . Tesla’s own company-compiled expectations predicted Q3 revenues of $28.3 billion.

The earnings come on the heels of a disappointing Q3 sales report , in which Tesla reported a 2.1 percent drop in customer deliveries compared to the blockbuster third quarter of 2025. (For a direct-to-consumer company like Tesla, deliveries are a proxy for sales.) The drop in sales was widely expected thanks to the expiration of the $7,500 federal tax credit for electric vehicles on September 30, 2025. Elon Musk himself said that the company was in for “a few rough quarters” thanks to the expiring incentive and other macroeconomic factors.

Tesla reported automotive revenues of $20.5 billion, a 3 percent decrease year over year — a sign that the company’s car business is floundering after the elimination of the tax credit. But there were troubling signs for Tesla’s other businesses too; the company reported $2.9 billion in energy generation and storage revenue, a staggering 16 percent drop year over year. “Services and other revenue,” such as money the company takes in from EV charging, maintenance, parts, and insurance, was up 33 percent to $4.6 billion – a rare bright spot in an otherwise dour earnings report.

Tesla’s capital spending — also known as capex — soared 110 percent year over year to $4.7 billion this quarter, as the company continue to pour money into AI, autonomous vehicles, and robotics. Musk has said to expect “a massive capex year” of at least $25 billion in capital spending as Tesla continues to transition into an AI and robotics company.

Operarting expenses — the day to day costs of running Tesla’s business — was up 39 percent year over year to $4.8 billion, while its income from operations — the profit Tesla generates from those day-to-day dealings — was down 56 percent year over year to just $718 million.

On the brighter side, Tesla reported a free cash flow of $1.5 billion, after dipping into negative territory last year. Still, that figure represents a 62 percent drop year over year, a sign that Tesla’s operating revenues were still struggling to cover its capital expenditures.

The possibility of a Tesla-SpaceX merger gained new momentum after Musk’s revelation this week that the two companies had formed special committees to discuss the possibility. Musk said a merger would be a “good idea,” even though he claimed he wouldn’t be involved in the process.

Beyond merger talks, this past quarter also saw the highly anticipated re-reveal of the next-generation Tesla Roadster , nine years after it was initially announced. The demo in Waco, Texas, featured a redesigned two-seat prototype flying and flipping through the air using cold-gas thrusters provided by SpaceX. While the event generated its own cottage industry of online reactions, it did little to asauge skeptics that the vehicle would actually go into production in 2028, as promised.
